decision.title: EXI 1.0 and Canonical EXI: two codecs at the data model boundary, the exi output method, our own DEFLATE (owner)
decision.summary: sxml reads and writes all of EXI 1.0 and Canonical EXI through a decoder of tree builder events and an encoder over trees (exi.h), with the output method exi:exi, the functions exi:serialize and exi:parse in urn:sxml:exi, schemaId through the resolver, its own DEFLATE, and EXIficient as the oracle of checked-in golden streams.

body.p: Recorded 2026-11-27 at the owner's word: "Full EXI with compression, write our own DEFLATE, go ahead, drive this to completion", after a spike of a binary storage format (spikes/sqlite-xml/, commit 8061ee002) and a sketch the owner accepted, with the namespace urn:sxml:exi. Phase 8 () carries it out; release 0.3.0 ships it.

item.p: Whom it serves: users who exchange XML with systems that speak EXI (vehicle-to-grid charging, smart-energy and IoT protocols use schema-informed EXI), users who sign XML in a canonical binary form, and users who want XML smaller on the wire. No other XQuery or XSLT processor has EXI (none found in a search, 2026-11-27).

The standards: Efficient XML Interchange (EXI) Format 1.0 (Second Edition), W3C Recommendation 11 February 2014, all of it: the four alignments, every option, built-in and schema-informed grammars; Canonical EXI, W3C Recommendation 7 June 2018. The EXI Profile is not in this phase. Compression uses DEFLATE (RFC 1951), and sxml writes its own encoder and decoder of it, from the RFC, with no third-party code.

Two codecs at the boundary of the data model (include/sxml/exi.h). sxml_exi_decoder reads a stream and sends tree builder events, as sxml_xml_parser does, so the result is an ordinary arena tree. sxml_exi_encoder walks any tree and writes to an sxml_output_stream, as the serializer does. Nothing in the evaluator changes. One grammar machine serves both directions; schema-informed grammars are built from the compiled schema of schema.h (its components in src/schema_internal.h), so sxml's XSD 1.1 implementation is the one schema model.

The data model and EXI: the encoder writes names, prefixes and namespace declarations (an element's in-scope namespaces its parent lacks), attributes, text, comments and processing instructions as the fidelity options allow. It writes no type annotations: a schema-informed stream types its values by its grammars. The decoder builds untyped nodes; validating them is the caller's. A tree has no DTD and no entity references, so the encoder writes none and the decoder ignores a DT event's contents and refuses an ER event.

Names: functions, the output method, its parameters and errors in urn:sxml:exi, predeclared as exi (SXML_NAMESPACE_EXI). The EXI options are the W3C's own, the options document in http://www.w3.org/2009/exi (SXML_NAMESPACE_EXI_FORMAT), with no predeclared prefix, since sxml gives exi to its own namespace; a W3C namespace gets no names W3C did not define.

Serialization: Serialization 4.0 lets method be a QName in a namespace, an implementation-defined method that may skip the phases that make octets from characters (its sections 3 and 4). So EXI is the method exi:exi (SXML_SERIALIZATION_METHOD_EXI), with namespaced parameters (exi:options, an exi:header element; exi:include-cookie, exi:include-options, exi:include-schema-id; exi:omit-options-document, exi:utc-time; exi:self-contained-elements), and Serialization's canonical parameter means Canonical EXI for it. XQuery output declarations, xsl:output, xsl:result-document, the command's --method and the bindings' serializers all reach it. fn:serialize returns a string and skips encoding (F&O 4.0, 17.2.3), so with this method it raises SEPM0016.

Functions: exi:serialize($input as item()*, $options as map(*)? := {}) as xs:base64Binary (the method's bytes, its options the method's parameters by local name) and exi:parse($stream as xs:base64Binary?, $options as map(*)? := {}) as document-node()? (the options for a stream whose header has none). fn:parse-xml keeps taking XML text only: choosing a format from the bytes is guessing.

Schemas by schemaId: a stream's schemaId is resolved through the processor's resource resolver, as a new kind SXML_RESOURCE_KIND_EXI_SCHEMA, and the compiled schema is kept per schemaId (sxml_processor_exi_schema_resolver).

The command (packet 8.14): sxml encode FILE writes an EXI stream, sxml decode FILE writes XML text, with the options as flags; --input-format=xml|exi on the commands that read a document. encode refuses to write to a terminal.

Bindings: the host shim gets an encode and a decode call; the JavaScript package processor.encodeEXI(value, options) and processor.parseEXI(bytes, options). Swift and Kotlin are paused () and get their methods when they resume.
Untrusted streams: the decoder bounds depth, decoded content bytes (and so DEFLATE expansion) and learned productions (sxml_exi_limits), and every decoder entry point gets a fuzzer.

Verification: EXIficient 1.0.4, the implementation of the EXI working group's editors, is the oracle, run only to make test data (tools/exi-oracle/). Its golden streams (tests/exi/: a sample of the vendored suites and handmade documents, crossed with option sets that cover every option) are checked in, so the tests need no Java. Each packet ratchets tests/exi/passing.txt: a case that passed must keep passing. Decoding is checked against EXIficient's decoding of the same stream, encoding byte for byte against EXIficient's stream (DEFLATE output aside, which may differ and is checked by decoding).
